context.//baseCapacity: Always-on reserved Macs = concurrent build slots. Each instance bills ~$25-30/day whether idle or busy; builds beyond the count QUEUE (ON_DEMAND is unavailable for MAC_ARM). Size to PEAK concurrency, not headcount. Default 1 (sequential).
context.//queuedTimeoutMinutes: Max minutes a build may sit QUEUED before CodeBuild fails it. CodeBuild's own default is 8h, which turns a wedged/disk-full Mac into a build that silently never starts. One reserved Mac serializes builds at ~10-15 min each, so 60 is about a four-deep real queue; raise it if you run deliberately deep queues. Allowed 5-480 (clamped).
context.//fleetStallMinutes: Minutes a build may be QUEUED with NOTHING running on the same fleet before ios_test calls that fleet stalled and refuses to enqueue (INSUFFICIENT_CAPACITY; force:true overrides). Read by the Lambda as FLEET_STALL_MINUTES. A stall has two causes - a starved build (the instance is alive and ran something within this window; CodeBuild's scheduler just skipped the queued build) or a wedged instance (nothing ran in a long time: unhealthy / out of disk) - and the Lambda reports which as stall_kind, since only the second one justifies recycling the fleet.
context.//vpc: OPTIONAL — set these to run builds inside your VPC (reach private Nexus, internal validation services). Leave empty for no VPC. subnetIds/securityGroupIds are comma-separated.
context.//createVpcEndpoints: When VPC mode is on, also create S3 + CloudWatch Logs + CodeBuild VPC endpoints so a private no-NAT subnet works. Set false if your VPC already has a NAT gateway.
